gaps.sentence: ___ the roadworks, the coach still arrived ahead of schedule.
Not only ___ the tickets cost more, but they sold out in minutes.
gaps.explanation: After fronted 'Not only', auxiliary inversion applies: Not only did the tickets cost more.

gaps.sentence: Insure the camera ___ it gets damaged in transit.
gaps.explanation: 'In case it gets damaged' = as a precaution against damage.

gaps.sentence: ___ the weather improves, the crossing will be cancelled.
gaps.explanation: Unless = if the weather doesn't improve — matching the cancellation.

gaps.sentence: The negotiations dragged on for months, but they ___ collapsed.
gaps.explanation: 'Eventually' signals the outcome after much delay.

gaps.sentence: ___ the criticism, the festival has been renewed for three more years.
gaps.explanation: 'In spite of' + noun phrase concedes the criticism.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: I know exactly what the risks are. ___, I'm going anyway.
gaps.hint: doing it in spite of risk
